newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WITNESS IN MATCH-FIXING CASE REMAINS IN CUSTODY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WITNESS IN MATCH-FIXING CASE REMAINS IN CUSTODY.

text.p: The main prosecution witness in the pending match-fixing trial of goakleeper Bruce Grobbelaar and two other soccer stars was spending a second night in custody on Wednesday.
Magistrates agreed to an application by police for a warrant of further detention for 37-year-old Zimbabwean businessman Chris Vincent, who was arrested on Tuesday.
A police spokesman said the warrant was granted by magistrates at Aldershot, 60 kms from London, without charge so further inquiries could be made by police.
The warrant allows police to continue to detain Vincent until midnight on Thursday.
Police have declined to give any details about the arrest of Vincent except to say he is being detained in connection with matters relating to the Grobbelaar inquiry.

Vincent, who came to Britain in 1989, is due to give evidence in the trial in January of Grobbelaar, the former Liverpool and Southampton goalkeeper who is now with Plymouth and coaching the Zimbabwe national squad, and Wimbledon keeper Hans Segers and former Aston Villa striker John Fashanu.
The three men, together with Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim, were arrested last year after a police investigation into match-fixing allegations.
They have denied the allegations and were committed for trial last March. The case against them is scheduled to be heard next January at Winchester Crown Court.
